'''Susan Ustin''' is an American earth scientist who is the Distinguished Professor of Environmental Resource Science at the [[John Muir]] Institute for the Environment, [[University of California, Davis]]. Her research makes use of remote sensing technology to understand the characteristics of plant communities.

== Early life and education ==
Ustin is from [[Eugene, Oregon]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|date=2018-01-04|title=Pioneer at UC Davis launched new field of study|url=https://www.davisenterprise.com/news/local/ucd/pioneer-at-uc-davis-launched-new-field-of-study/|access-date=2020-12-04|website=Davis Enterprise}}</ref> After graduating from high school in 1961, Ustin moved to [[San Francisco]] with her friends.<ref name=":1" /> She was inspired by the city's activism, in particular the [[civil rights movement]] and environmental advocates.<ref name=":1" /> She first studied biology at [[California State University, East Bay]], specialising in plant physiological ecology.<ref name=":1" /><ref name="lawr.ucdavis.edu">{{Cite web|title=Department of Land, Air and Water Resources - UC Davis :: Ustin, Susan L.|url=http://lawr.ucdavis.edu/people/emeriti/ustin-susan|access-date=2020-12-04|website=lawr.ucdavis.edu}}</ref> She remained there for a master's degree, before moving to the [[University of California, Davis]] for her doctoral degree.<ref>{{Cite web|title=International Workshop on Sensors and Small Satellite Technology for Disaster Management – SSTDM 2016 {{!}} Amrita Vishwa Vidyapeetham|url=https://www.amrita.edu/event/sstdm2016/susan-ustin|access-date=2020-12-04|website=www.amrita.edu}}</ref> Alongside her doctoral research Ustin started working at the [[Jet Propulsion Laboratory]].<ref name=":1" /> She started working on remote sensing technology in the early 1980s, when the field was then in its infancy.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Stumbos|first=John|date=2017-10-02|title=Remote Sensing Pioneer|url=https://caes.ucdavis.edu/news/awards-and-honors/2017/remote-sensing-pioneer|access-date=2020-12-04|website=College of Agricultural and Environmental Sciences|language=en}}</ref>

== Research and career ==
Her work considers [[remote sensing]] of environmental and landscape properties, making use of hyperspectral analysis and thermal scanners.<ref name="lawr.ucdavis.edu"/> Remote sensing has since been used to monitor natural disasters, study climate changes and monitor air pollution.<ref name=":1" /> Over the course of her career, Ustin made use of remote sensing data from five different continents, including tracking the impacts of agriculture on forests and monitoring invasive plant species.<ref name=":1" />

Ustin held several positions at University of California, Davis, including serving as Director of both the Center for Spatial Technology and Remote Sensing and the John Muir Institute of the Environment.<ref name=":1" /><ref>{{Cite web|title=Loop {{!}} Susan L. Ustin|url=https://loop.frontiersin.org/people/294910/overview|access-date=2020-12-04|website=loop.frontiersin.org}}</ref> She worked with [[NASA]] to build space-based imaging spectrometers.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Susan Ustin {{!}} NASA Airborne Science Program|url=https://airbornescience.nasa.gov/person/Susan_Ustin|access-date=2020-12-04|website=airbornescience.nasa.gov|language=en}}</ref>

In 2020 Ustin was elected to the [[Ecological Society of America]]. Her citation read, <blockquote>“Elected for research pioneering the use of remote sensing technology for detecting changes in plant community characteristics, biological diversity, and land use, and for her continued influence on the field,”.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=ESA Fellows – The Ecological Society of America|url=https://www.esa.org/programs/fellows-program/esa-fellows/|access-date=2020-12-04|language=en-US}}</ref></blockquote>
